newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Zagrebacka Banka cuts kuna rates.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Zagrebacka Banka cuts kuna rates.

text.p: Croatia's leading commercial bank, Zagrebacka Banka, said on Wednesday it would cut its kuna lending rates by another percentage point from November 1.
The rate on loans to prime clients will be 16 instead of 17 percent and 20 percent to other company borrowers, it said in a news release.
The short-term credit to citizens through their current accounts will now be granted at 17 percent.
Also effective from November, the bank will cut by one percentage point to 8.5-10.5 percent the interest paid on all kuna deposits of over one month.

Other short-term deposit rates will be trimmed 50 basis points to between 2.5 percent for companies' sight deposits and 4.0 percent on citizens' three-week savings. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-41-4557075
